title: Test-Ready Basics (A1/A2)
description: Essential grammatical foundations: grammatical gender (der, die, das), accusative case, and verb conjugations.

items.prompt: Which definite article is used for masculine nouns in the nominative case?
items.explanation: German has three grammatical genders: masculine (der), feminine (die), and neuter (das).

items.prompt: In the accusative case (direct object), 'der' changes to:
items.explanation: Only masculine articles change in the accusative case: der -> den (die and das remain unchanged).
The irregular present tense conjugation is: ich habe, du hast, er/sie/es hat.

items.prompt: Where does the conjugated finite verb sit in a standard German main clause?
items.explanation: The V2 (Verb Second) rule is a fundamental pillar of German main clause syntax.

items.prompt: Which preposition takes the dative case to express origin ('from')?
items.explanation: 'aus' is a dative preposition expressing origin or coming out of a place (e.g. aus Bangladesch, aus dem Zimmer).
